newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden sees wage rises as key to unemployment goal.
newsitem.headline: Sweden sees wage rises as key to unemployment goal.

text.p: The level of Swedish wage rises were a key factor in the government's forecast to cut unemployment to 4.5 percent by 2000, Sweden's Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
"We expect wage increases in the years 1999 and 2000 won't exceed 3.5 percent annually even if we get a large reduction in unemployment," Ministry spokesman Ingemar Hansson said.
"If wages rise faster, we won't be able to meet the unemployment target."
He said there was great uncertainty about whether wage formation will work as well as the government has assumed.
Unemployment stood at 8.4 percent in March and the minority Social Democratic government has pledged to halve it to four percent in 2000.
In Sweden's supplementary budget released on Tuesday the government forecast unemployment being reduced to 4.5 percent at the turn of the century.
The government forecast average unemployment at 7.9 percent in 1997, falling to 7.1 percent in 1998 and 5.6 percent in 1999.
